climate.koppen_name: Temperate, no dry season, warm summer

climate: Seasons this mild ripen Riesling, Pinot Noir, Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc and Sémillon fully without cooking off their freshness.
Rain picks up at harvest. Growers race to pick before rot sets in, and vintages vary more.

soil.rock: Schist, slate and gneiss break into stony, free-draining soil that holds the day's heat. Schist is rich in magnesium and potassium but poor in organic matter and nitrogen. Sand is warm and airy. It drains fast but holds little water, and phylloxera does not thrive in it.
soil.top: The topsoil drains well and still stores water for dry spells, so vines grow evenly. Its pH is close to neutral, so vines take up the nutrients they need easily.

land: Much of it is steep. Cold air and rain run off, so frost and waterlogging are rare and soils stay thin, keeping yields low. Steep rows are slow and costly to work, often by hand.
Faces the morning sun. Early light dries the dew, which cuts disease, and the grapes are spared the hottest afternoon sun.
